artboards.title: A · The field, rival by rival (chosen)
B · Week by week, every rival at once

annotations.text:
The Market area: two ways to draw it, replacing today's Auction insights, Week by week (the trends chart) and The market cards. Both make it one section, Rivals, with the market's four public figures and your own share on top, because the market card alone was too small to fill a section (the owner agreed, 2026-09-15). The switch top right shows it after week 6, and after week 9, when month 3's budgets take effect.
Real figures from the engine: seed 1, Vella & Co. at mid-price performance, the makeover canvas's keywords. Only what a player may see (R3): each rival's name, site and ad, and your own Auction Insights against them; never a rival's spend, bids or results. At week 9 the whole market spent ₹3,02,140 against ₹4,18,404 the week before, and only Marlow moved five points in your auctions (45% to 40%); the biggest moves came at week 6, Torvi down from 80% to 56% and Marlow up from 15% to 36%.

Chosen by the owner, 2026-09-15. A · The field, rival by rival. Each rival you meet is a card: how often they are in your auctions this week, with every week so far as small bars, their ad as searchers see it, and who comes out above. Sorted by how often you meet; one you never meet is a line at the end.
For: rivals as players, which is the brief: names and ads you come to recognise, and each one's story on its own card.
Against: long, seven cards; comparing two rivals means reading two cards.

B · Week by week, every rival at once. One grid: a row a rival, a bar a week, for the figure you pick (in your auctions, above you, or you outrank them). Pick a row and that rival's ad and this week's figures sit beside it.
For: compact, and a change over the weeks is seen across every rival at once.
Against: a rival is a row of bars until picked; the ads, the part that makes them players, are one at a time.

For you to decide, found while mapping today's cards:
1. A results page for one particular search (who appeared, in what order) is listed in the makeover design as your decision: the public view does not carry it, so it would change what players may know and needs a DECISIONS entry first. Neither option draws it.
2. Round 0's notes on where each rival sits are not kept after round 0 (the end reveal asks again). Showing them on each rival here would change the save. Neither option draws them.
3. Today's trends chart also plots impression share, top of page and absolute top for everyone. Neither option keeps those three for rivals: they are each rival's own figures, easy to read as a leaderboard, which the chart itself warns against ("most visible is not winning"). Your own share is on the top card.
4. Today's reading names the rival "above you most often when you meet" by that rate alone, so it can name one you hardly meet: after week 9, Halcyon, above you 74% of the time in the 2% of your auctions it is in. Both options name instead the rival above you in the most of all the auctions you show in (how often you meet, times how often it is above): Kestrel, 67% after week 9, 66% after week 6.
5. A second read of these mock-ups fixed five wordings before this commit: "your auctions" meant two different things; a rival "may spend a hundredth of what you do" read as a fact about that rival; nothing said why above-you and you-outrank can read 100% and 43% on one card; a median click of Rs 9.68 against Rs 9.40 printed as Rs 10 against Rs 9; and a move was judged on unrounded figures while the screen printed rounded ones (Marlow, 45% to 40%, "did not move").
6. The chart's sentences are still written into ui/chart.js rather than ui/words; the rebuild moves them.
